standard.title: Locate key information in familiar texts
standard.description: locate, with support, key information in familiar texts, and respond using gestures, images, words and formulaic phrases
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise meaning in target language input with support using gesture, visual cues and context (AC9LSF01). They have no prior experience locating specific information in structured target language texts or categorising information from texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate key information in familiar spoken, written and multimodal target language texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and formulaic phrases.

nodes.label: Locating key words and phrases in familiar texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can locate key words and phrases in familiar target language texts using context, pictures, intonation and known vocabulary as cues.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three key words or phrases in a familiar text using context, pictures or intonation as support.
nodes.typical_width: Listen for and identify key words and phrases in simple spoken, print and digital texts — stories, songs, rhymes, simple dialogues; use intonation patterns to assist comprehension; participate in shared reading using pictures, keywords and contextual clues to predict meaning; demonstrate comprehension by labelling, matching, drawing or selecting.
wider: Sequence events from a familiar text using images or key words — demonstrating comprehension beyond isolated word recognition
Notice how gesture and body language in target language texts carry meaning — and compare with gesture conventions from other languages known to the class
nodes.hinge_reason: Locating key information in texts is the prerequisite for all reading comprehension and text response work. Students who can only recognise isolated words cannot extract meaning from connected text — which is required for the categorisation and response work in node 2.

response_modes.reason: Text comprehension strategies develop through exposure to varied familiar text types — stories, songs, rhymes, instructions — each presenting different contextual cue conditions.

success_criteria: Identifies at least three key words or phrases in a familiar text with support from pictures or context
Demonstrates comprehension through an appropriate response — labelling, matching, drawing, miming or selecting

nodes.label: Responding to texts and categorising information
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to familiar target language texts using varied response modes and begin to categorise information from texts using simple graphic organisers.
nodes.minimum_width: Respond to a familiar text using at least two response modes (e.g. gesture and words, image and phrase) and complete at least one simple categorisation task from text content.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to spoken, print and digital texts through play-acting, illustrating, movement and verbal response; answer simple questions about characters, places and objects; categorise information using graphic organisers — likes/dislikes, opposites, categories, similarities/differences; recognise that gesture and body language are integral to communication across languages including First Nations Australian languages.
wider: Create a bilingual graphic organiser from a text — categorising information in both the target language and English
Produce a simple spoken response to a text in the target language — not only gesture or image, but a formulaic phrase that communicates a reaction or finding

response_modes.reason: Response repertoire develops through varied response conditions — different text types, question types and response modes. Students who always respond in one mode do not develop the verbal response capacity needed at 3-4.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Moving from non-verbal to verbal text response — producing a formulaic phrase rather than only gesture or image — bridges to text creation at this band and the next.
success_criteria: Responds to a familiar text using at least two different response modes
Categorises at least four items from a text using a simple graphic organiser
